anomalies.title: Kernel slab memory leak
anomalies.hypothesis: A kernel subsystem is allocating 'kmalloc-256' objects without freeing them. Likely candidates: network socket buffers, crypto subsystem, or a loadable module.
recommended_actions: Run `cat /proc/slabinfo | grep kmalloc-256` over time to confirm growth rate
Inspect recently loaded modules for slab allocation patterns

anomalies.title: Active OOM condition

evidence.finding: OOM killer fired 3 time(s) between snapshots

anomalies.hypothesis: The system ran out of memory and the OOM killer terminated processes. This indicates severe memory pressure.
recommended_actions: Check `dmesg | grep -i oom` for killed process names
Investigate the largest memory consumers at the time of OOM
Consider increasing swap or reducing memory consumers

anomalies.title: Graphics/media memory leak (DMA-BUF + KGSL + process)

evidence.finding: KGSL GPU memory grew by 64.0 MB

anomalies.hypothesis: A graphics or media subsystem is accumulating GPU/display buffers. Common causes: surfaceflinger buffer leak, video decoder not releasing frames, camera HAL holding buffers.
recommended_actions: Check for unclosed EGL surfaces or unreleased MediaCodec buffers

anomalies.title: CMA exhaustion risk
anomalies.hypothesis: CMA usage is growing, which may exhaust contiguous memory available for camera, video, and ADSP subsystems.
recommended_actions: Identify which subsystem is consuming CMA (camera, video, ADSP)
Consider increasing CMA pool size if usage is legitimate
